newsitem.title: USA: Chart explaining TV rating system.
newsitem.headline: Chart explaining TV rating system.

text.p: The following chart shows the new ratings system unveiled Thursday by TV industry executives for their shows. It shows actual ratings -- such as TV-Y -- as well as broader explanation of the ratings.
TV-Y: All Children -- Programme contains themes and elements for a "very young audience," including children from ages 2-6.
TV-Y7: Directed to Older Children -- Ages 7 and up. Themes and elements in programme "may include mild physical or comedic violence, or may frighten" younger children.
TV-G: General Audience -- Suitable for all ages; programme has "little or no violence, no strong language and little or no sexual dialogue or situations."
TV-PG: Parental Guidance Suggested -- Programme may have "infrequent coarse language, limited violence, some suggestive sexual dialogue and situations."
TV-14: Parents Strongly Cautioned -- Programme may be unsuitable for children under 14 years old; may contain "sophisticated themes, sexual content, strong language and more intense violence."
TV-M: Mature Audience Only -- May be unsuitable for children younger than 17. Programme may contain "mature themes, profane language, graphic violence and explicit sexual content."
